title: Lovalingo
description: A translation tool for vibe coders using Lovable, Replit, Claude Code, and modern web builders.
body:
Lovalingo is a translation tool for vibe coders: people building web pages fast with Lovable, Replit, Claude Code, and other modern AI-first builders.

The problem is simple. Vibe-coded apps can get from idea to live page quickly, but translation is still annoying once the site has multiple routes, components, SEO pages, and product copy. Lovalingo is built to make those pages multilingual without turning the project into a manual i18n cleanup job.

## What it does

- Helps translate web pages built with Lovable, Replit, Claude Code, and React or Next.js stacks.
- Turns fast-built pages into multilingual surfaces without making the builder rewrite everything by hand.
- Supports localization basics like translated copy, routes, SEO pages, canonicals, sitemaps, and public route coverage.
- Gives builders an operational layer for projects, content, users, and translation workflows.
- Treats route coverage and metadata as part of the translation problem, not an afterthought.

## Why this project exists

AI builders make it easier to create a first version of a product, but they can also leave teams with messy content structures. Translation exposes that mess quickly. A landing page might be easy to translate, but a real site has guides, comparison pages, help pages, integrations, pricing, legal documents, middleware, sitemap behavior, and language-switcher edge cases.

Lovalingo is aimed at that messy middle. It is for builders who can ship fast but do not want every new locale to become a manual route audit.

## Recent work from local commits

The recent commits split across the package and the web surface. The package side clarified manifest coverage prompts, documented manifest maintenance for agents, and released `@lovalingo/lovalingo` 0.5.29.

The web side focused on route coverage, language-switcher recovery, locale fallback behavior, sitemap validation, production sitemap checks, GSC baseline records, legacy redirects, priority use-case SEO, and extractable answer content.

The May 14 pass restored a much broader public route set: about, comparisons, pricing, integrations, help pages, guides, MDX components, RSS, sitemap, middleware, theme support, and smoke tests. That turned the public site from a thin shell back into a more complete product surface.

## Product story

Lovalingo is not just “translate this string.” The more interesting product is a workflow that understands the shape of a website. Which routes exist? Which pages are public? Which metadata needs localized treatment? Which legacy routes need redirects? Which sitemap entries prove the translated surface is actually reachable?

That is why the public-route restoration matters. Translation quality does not help if half the site is unreachable, missing from the sitemap, or inconsistent across locales.

## Current direction

The next direction is deeper automation around route discovery, manifest maintenance, translation review, and SEO-safe publishing. The product should help builders keep multilingual sites healthy after the first translation pass, not only generate a one-time output.

## Public boundary

This page describes the public product and website work. It does not expose private customer content, credentials, account data, or unpublished translation datasets.
